summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: California fines Afterpay $2.7M
articles.description: The state imposed the penalty on Block’s buy now, pay later business after finding the company failed to assess customers’ ability to repay loans.

articles.title: Illinois fights for interchange law
articles.description: The state’s attorney general filed a brief in appellate court Monday stressing the invalidity of a federal move to stop the Illinois Interchange Fee Prohibition Act.

articles.title: Cap One pursues payments modernization
articles.description: The bank’s investments in real-time and cloud-based rails are letting it keep pace with technology advances, a top payments executive said.

articles.title: Adyen co-founder to step down
articles.description: “I feel my cycle is complete,” Pieter van der Does, also co-CEO, wrote after 20 years with Adyen. “This is the right moment for me to step down.”

articles.title: Payoneer gets conditional approval for trust bank
articles.description: The cross-border payments company, which applied for a trust charter in February, is one of several payments firms that sought a charter from the OCC this year.

articles.title: Intermex sues Western Union
articles.description: The long-time remittance provider walked away from a $500 million merger deal due to “buyer’s remorse,” Intermex alleged in a Tuesday lawsuit.

articles.title: PayPal’s new CFO lands big pay
articles.description: The digital payments player handed Claire Bramley, an HP alum, a $30 million pay package to take the chief financial officer post in February.

articles.title: Fed president pitches FedNow
articles.description: Jeff Schmid, who leads the Kansas City Federal Reserve, nudged credit union executives last week to adopt faster payment options, like FedNow.
